note: #172: head_sha is well-formed but names no commit in any clone, so it is ipso facto NOT an ancestor of origin/main — the ancestry leg fires (`merge-base --is-ancestor` exits non-zero, 'not an ancestor of origin/main') alongside the real-commit leg (`cat-file` on a phantom SHA). A synthetic SHA is used because the trap runs verify.py against the AMBIENT repo (vfbench.py cwd=ROOT): an isolated ancestry-only RED would need a commit present in every clone yet never on origin/main, and no such commit can be pinned (fresh clones hold only origin/main ancestors; a transient feature-branch SHA would couple the suite to unrelated branch merges/deletions). The ancestry leg is exercised end-to-end here; ISOLATED positive/negative coverage lives in tests/test_verify.py GitAuthorityChecks. head_sha = sha256('vf-bench non-ancestor fixture (#172)')[:40].
